content.markdown:
# MyLoop

A mobile game where players capture real-world territory by physically completing loops (walking). Territory is represented as H3 hexagonal cells (~65m resolution). Overlapping claims steal territory. City-wide daily leaderboards drive competition. Future: group/team play.

**Stack**: Flutter 3.44.0 (mobile/web) + .NET 10 minimal API (backend) + PostgreSQL 18 (geo) + pocketken.H3 (hex computation) + flutter_map + OSM tiles (map rendering) + ngrok (remote testing tunnel)

## Features


## Systems

sectionContent.What Is MyLoop?:
**MyLoop is a real-world territory capture game.** Players physically walk to claim hexagonal grid cells on a shared world map. Walk a loop → everything inside becomes yours. Others can steal your territory by walking through it — but you get notified and can reclaim.

Think: **Pokémon GO meets Risk meets Strava** — but instead of catching creatures or recording fitness, you're conquering and defending real geographic territory against other players in your city.

---
sectionContent.Core Gameplay Loop:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Open App] --> B[See Map with Territory]
    B --> C[Tap START JOURNEY]
    C --> D[Walk a Physical Loop]
    D --> E{Loop Detected?}
    E -->|Yes| F[STOP & CAPTURE]
    E -->|No| G[End Walk / Discard]
    F --> H[Server: Anti-Cheat Validation]
    H --> I[Server: H3 Hex Computation]
    I --> J[Server: Assign Ownership + Record Transfers]
    J --> K[Real-Time Broadcast to All Players in Area]
    K --> L[Push Notification to Victims]
    J --> M[Update Leaderboard Position]
    M --> B
```

**What makes it addictive:**
1. You SEE territory on the map — visceral ownership
2. Others can STEAL it — creates urgency to defend
3. Daily streaks + leaderboard rank — competitive drive
4. Physical activity required — can't cheat from couch (anti-cheat enforced)
5. Local competition — city-level leaderboards make it personal

---
sectionContent.1. Territory Capture (Core):
- Walk physically. GPS tracks your path at 5-second intervals.
- Close a loop (path endpoints within 50m) → all hexes inside the polygon are captured
- Trail cells (hexes you walk through) are always claimed regardless of loop
- Loop interior fill: closed polygon → H3 fill algorithm claims all hexes inside
- **Min walk: 200m.** Max area per claim: 5 km². Max 20 claims/day.
- 5-hour cooldown on captured cells (anti-grief: prevents instant re-steal)
- Last-writer-wins conflict model (physical presence = ownership)
- Stolen hexes logged for revenge tracking (who took what, when)
sectionContent.2. Real-Time Territory Updates (SignalR):
- WebSocket connection to `/hubs/territory` backend hub
- Connects ONCE on login (after Firebase auth), lives app-lifetime
- Players auto-subscribe to geographic regions (H3 resolution-3 parent cells, ~12km zones)
- Personal group subscription (`user_{userId}`) for private stat deltas
- When anyone claims territory nearby, your map updates instantly via `HexOwnershipChanged` event
- Personal pushes: `UserStatsDelta`, `XpDelta`, `MissionDelta`, `AchievementUnlocked`
- Victim pushes: `UserStatsDelta` with decremented hexCount when hex is stolen
- Reconnection logic with automatic re-subscription + full re-hydrate
- Region subscription updates dynamically as you pan the map
- No [Authorize] on hub class — supports mixed auth (public regions + authenticated personal groups)
- Hub validates token in `JoinUserGroup` before adding to personal group
sectionContent.3. Anti-Cheat System (3-Layer Server Val:
- **Speed check**: Consecutive GPS points must be physically walkable (≤30 km/h, ≤60m per 5s interval). Allows 5% violations for GPS drift.
- **Duration check**: Path must have ≥50% of expected GPS samples for the distance walked
- **Smoothness check**: Bearing standard deviation must be >2°. Real GPS has natural jitter; spoofed linear paths are suspiciously smooth.
- **Batch-step path coverage (abb321a)**: the real-time batch-step claim path (the PRIMARY way players claim) is now validated too, via `ValidateConsecutivePoints` — each GPS hop is bounded by `MaxSpeed × elapsedTime + 30m` drift margin using real `CapturedAt` timestamps; rejected with `400 Anti-cheat: …` over the same 5% tolerance. Previously only loop claims were checked, so a spoofer could teleport on the batch path.
- Rejects GPS spoofers, car drivers disguised as walkers, teleportation hacks
sectionContent.4. Push Notifications (Territory Theft A:
- Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) on iOS + Android
- Triggered when another player steals your hexes
- Message: "Territory Under Attack! ⚔️ — {PlayerName} captured {N} of your hexes!"
- Creates urgency to defend → drives re-engagement
sectionContent.5. Leaderboard System:
- **Scopes**: City / Country / World
- Daily refresh: ranks all players by owned hex count
- Top 20 displayed + your own rank always visible
- Achievement counters increment on rank thresholds (top 3/10/100/1000)
- 7-day history retention for trend analysis
sectionContent.6. Progression System (Daily Missions +:
**XP & Levels:**
- XP earned from: hex capture (10), hex steal (25), per km (50), streak bonus (20), all-missions bonus (100), individual mission completion, achievement unlocks (25–1000)
- Level formula: `(n-1)² × 100` XP per level. Level 10 = 8,100 XP. Level 50 = 240,100 XP.
- Level displayed in UI, used for achievement thresholds

**Daily Missions (3 per day, adaptive):**
- Generated per user per day using deterministic seed (same missions on reload)
- 6 types: CaptureHexes, WalkDistance, StealHex, ExploreNewArea, MaintainStreak, CaptureInOneWalk
- Adaptive difficulty: Player tier (Newcomer/Regular/Veteran/Elite) × behavior weights → weighted selection
- All-missions bonus: 100 XP when all 3 complete in one day
- Progress tracked in real-time during walks

**Achievements (30 permanent badges, 7 categories):**
- Capture (7): 1→5000 hexes captured
- Streak (6): 3→100 consecutive days
- Distance (5): 1→500 km walked
- PvP (4): 1→100 hexes stolen from others
- Level (4): Level 5/10/25/50
- Leaderboard (2): 1/10 top-3 finishes
- Missions (3): 7/30/100 all-missions-complete days
- Unlocked permanently, award XP (25–1000), shown as badges on profile
- Convergence loop handles cascading unlocks (achievement XP → level → level achievement)

**Architecture:**
- Single-save-point pattern: missions + achievements + XP all saved in one `SaveChangesAsync`
- Concurrent-safe: `DbUpdateException` caught at save point, conflicting achievement inserts detached
- Denormalized counters: `TotalHexesStolen`, `AllMissionsCompleteDays` on User entity
- Checked on every hex capture (negligible perf: 30 int comparisons)
sectionContent.7. Revenge System:
- See who stole your hexes (last 30 days)
- Grouped by attacker — "Player X stole 47 hexes from you"
- Navigate back to stolen locations and reclaim
- 7-day revenge window for priority recapture
sectionContent.8. Walk History:
- Paginated list of all past claims
- Shows: cell count, area captured, date
- Infinite scroll with lazy loading
sectionContent.9. User Profiles:
- Emoji-based avatar system (50+ avatars)
- 8 territory colors (player's hexes render in their color)
- Public profile viewable from leaderboard (stats, rank, title, tier badge)
- Account deletion (GDPR compliance)
sectionContent.10. Map Visualization:
- **Dual themes**: Satellite (ESRI World Imagery) + Dark (CartoDB)
- **Hex rendering**: User hexes at 20% opacity fill + solid border, other players' hexes colored by owner
- **Tap-to-inspect**: Tap any hex → see owner, claim date, ownership history
- **Follow mode**: Auto-center on GPS, toggle with re-center button
- **Wide-area preload**: Load all user hexes + ~1km viewport on app open
- **Active walk trail**: Green polyline showing current GPS path
sectionContent.11. Bot Territory System (Cold Start):
- Pre-populated territory in major cities (Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, London, NYC, Tokyo)
- 10 bot players with realistic hex clusters (~200 hexes each)
- Creates immediate competition for day-1 players in supported cities
- Bots have varied stats, colors, and territory sizes

---
sectionContent.Stack:
| Layer | Technology | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Mobile | Flutter 3.44 / Dart 3.12 | Single codebase for iOS + Android. Fast iteration. |
| Backend | .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core) | High-performance, SignalR built-in, EF Core for DB. |
| Database | PostgreSQL 18 | GiST spatial indexes, reliable, free. |
| Spatial Grid | H3 (Uber) via pocketken.H3 | Global hexagonal grid. Hierarchical (res 3→11). Consistent cell sizes worldwide. |
| Real-Time | SignalR (WebSocket) | Built into ASP.NET, auto-fallback to long-polling, group-based broadcast. |
| Auth | Firebase Authentication | Free, handles Google/Apple OAuth, JWT tokens. |
| Push | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Cross-platform, free tier covers millions of messages. |
| Map Tiles | ESRI + CartoDB (free) | No API key, no billing, unlimited tiles. |
| State Mgmt | Riverpod 3.x | Modern Flutter state. Compile-safe. Reactive. |
| Navigation | go_router + ShellRoute | URL-based, tab persistence via IndexedStack. |
| Dev Tunnel | ngrok | Mobile testing without same-WiFi. Instant HTTPS. |
sectionContent.Backend Architecture (SOLID):
```
Controllers (thin) → Services (business logic) → EF Core (data access)
         ↑                    ↑                         ↑
   Input validation    Interface-backed         PostgreSQL
   Route → Service     Constructor-injected     GiST spatial index
   ≤20 lines          ≤40 lines per method
```

**Services**:
- `TerritoryService` — Claim processing pipeline (validate → compute → assign → push deltas → broadcast)
- `HexGridService` — H3 computation (point-to-cell, loop extraction, polygon fill, boundaries)
- `PathValidationService` — Anti-cheat (speed, duration, smoothness checks)
- `TerritoryNotifier` — SignalR push to region groups (public hex changes) + user groups (personal deltas)
- `PushNotificationService` — FCM push to victims
- `UserService` — Registration, profile CRUD, account deletion
- `LeaderboardService` — Daily rank computation, scoped queries
- `MissionService` — Daily mission generation, progress recording, XP awarding
- `AchievementService` — Achievement checking with convergence loop
- `GeoService` — Haversine distance, bearing calculations
- `ValidationService` — Input sanitization

sectionContent.Communication Patterns:
| Pattern | Technology | Data Flow | Use Case |
|---------|-----------|-----------|----------|
| **Request/Response** | HTTP REST (Dio + ASP.NET) | Mobile → API → DB → Mobile | Claims, viewport queries, profiles, leaderboard |
| **Real-Time Push (Public)** | SignalR WebSocket | Server → Region Group Clients | Territory ownership changes (instant map updates) |
| **Real-Time Push (Personal)** | SignalR WebSocket | Server → User Group Client | Stats/XP/Mission/Achievement deltas after claims |
| **Background Push** | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Server → FCM → Device OS → App | "Your hex was stolen" notifications (even when app closed) |
| **Auth Token** | Firebase JWT | Mobile → Firebase → JWT → API (Bearer header) | Every authenticated API call (auto-refresh every hour) |
| **Geo Subscription** | SignalR Groups | Client joins H3 parent cell groups | Only receive broadcasts for your visible map area |
sectionContent.Real-Time State Architecture (Delta-Push:
**Design principle**: HTTP for writes (reliable), SignalR for pushing consequences (fast).

```
                  SignalR /hubs/territory
                  ──────────────────────
App login ────► Connect ONCE, lives forever (not per-screen)
              ├─► JoinUserGroup("user_{myId}")     ← personal events
              ├─► JoinRegion(parentCellId)          ← visible map area
              └─► Auto-reconnect + re-hydrate on resume
```

**Event Flow After Step Claim:**
```
1. Client HTTP POSTs /api/claims/step (reliable, retryable)
2. Server processes: hex ownership + XP + missions + achievements (single transaction)
3. Server pushes (AFTER SaveChanges succeeds):
   → Region group: HexOwnershipChanged (map update for all nearby)
   → Claiming user group: UserStatsDelta + XpDelta + MissionDelta + AchievementUnlocked
   → Victim user group (if steal): UserStatsDelta (hexCount--)
   → FCM to victim (background notification)
4. Client applies deltas to state slices — no extra HTTP round-trip
```

**State Slices (Flutter — 5 independent Notifiers, ALL IMPLEMENTED):**

| Slice | Provider | Data | Hydrated On Login | Updated Via Push |
|-------|----------|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Profile | `profileSliceProvider` | hexCount, streak, distanceKm, rank, totalHexesCaptured, totalHexesStolen | ✅ | `UserStatsDelta` |
| XP | `xpSliceProvider` | totalXp, level, progressXp, neededXp, progressPercent | ✅ | `XpDelta` |
| Missions | `missionsSliceProvider` | 3 daily missions + progress, allComplete | ✅ | `MissionDelta` |
| Achievements | `achievementsSliceProvider` | unlocked list | ✅ | `AchievementUnlocked` |
| Exploration | `explorationSliceProvider` | neighborhood coverage % | ✅ | On-demand only (no push) |

**Hydration orchestrator**: `hydrateAllSlices(ref)` in `hydration.dart` — calls `GET /api/users/{id}/game-state`, distributes response to all 5 slice notifiers via `.hydrate()` method.

**Deleted**: `game_state.dart` (monolithic GameState + GameStateNotifier) — replaced by 5 independent slices.
sectionContent.Algorithm Deep-Dive: Claim Processing:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant M as Mobile
    participant API as .NET API
    participant PV as PathValidator
    participant HG as HexGridService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant SR as SignalR Hub
    participant FCM as Firebase Push

    M->>API: POST /api/claims {userId, path[][]}
    API->>PV: Validate(path) — speed, duration, smoothness
    PV-->>API: valid (or reject with reason)
    API->>HG: ComputeCapturedCells(path)
    Note over HG: 1. Trail cells (path intersects)
    Note over HG: 2. Extract loops (closure ≤50m)
    Note over HG: 3. Fill polygon interior (H3.Fill)
    Note over HG: 4. Deduplicate overlaps (>80%)
    HG-->>API: Dict cellId → boundary
    API->>DB: BEGIN TRANSACTION
    Note over API,DB: Batch-load existing cells (single query)
    Note over API,DB: Skip cooldown cells, skip self-owned
    Note over API,DB: Upsert cells + create transfers
    Note over API,DB: Update user stats (hex count, streak, distance)
    Note over API,DB: Decrement victim hex counts
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    API-->>M: ClaimResponse {cellCount, area, boundaries}
    API->>SR: BroadcastOwnershipChanges(region groups)
    SR-->>M: HexOwnershipChanged event (all nearby clients)
    API->>FCM: NotifyVictimsOfTheft(grouped by victim)
    FCM-->>M: Push: Territory Under Attack!
```
sectionContent.H3 Hexagonal Grid System:
**Why H3?**
- Uniform hexagons worldwide (unlike lat/lng grid which distorts at poles)
- Hierarchical: res-11 cells (25m edge) nest into res-3 parents (~12km zones)
- Polygon fill: given any closed shape, H3 returns all hexes inside it
- Deduplication: each hex has ONE globally unique ID — no overlap ambiguity
- Spatial grouping: parent cells naturally partition the world into SignalR broadcast zones

**Resolution 11 choice:**
- Edge length: ~25-29m
- Area per cell: ~2,150 m²
- Feels earnable: a typical city block walk captures 20-50 hexes
- Not too granular (res 12+ would require excessive walking for visible territory)
sectionContent.GPS & Location Strategy:
- **Tracking only during active capture** — battery-friendly, privacy-respecting
- **5-second sampling interval** — enough resolution for path shape, not excessive data
- **Accuracy filter**: Reject readings with accuracy > 25m
- **Speed-aware noise floor**: Stationary = 10-25m clamp, moving = 6-20m clamp
- **Distance filter**: Only record if displacement > 10m (prevent GPS drift accumulation)
- **"When In Use" permission only** — required for Apple App Store approval

---
sectionContent.Game Constants:
| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| H3 Resolution | 11 | ~25m edge. Walkable, visible, not too granular. |
| H3 Parent Resolution | 3 | ~12km zones. Good SignalR broadcast scope. |
| Min GPS Points | 10 | Path must have substance |
| Min Walk Distance | 200m | Prevents trivial tap-and-claim abuse |
| Max Claim Area | 5 km² | Prevents city-wide single-claim exploits |
| Max Claims/Day | 20 | Fair daily cap |
| Cell Cooldown | 5 hours | Anti-grief window |
| Loop Closure Distance | 50m | How close endpoints must be to detect a loop |
| Min Loop Points | 20 | Loop must represent real walking |
| Min Fill Area | 5,000 m² | Ignore tiny interior loops |
| Overlap Dedup Threshold | 80% | Skip near-duplicate polygons |
| Max Speed (Anti-Cheat) | 30 km/h (8.33 m/s) | Walking/jogging speed ceiling |
| Speed Violation Tolerance | 5% | Allow GPS jumps |
| Bearing StdDev Minimum | 2° | Catch linear spoofed paths |
| Max Viewport Cells | 500 | API response size cap |
| Max User Territory Cells | 2,000 | Per-user query limit |
| Leaderboard Top Count | 20 | Visible ranks |
| Revenge Window | 7 days | Time to reclaim stolen hexes |
| XP per Hex Captured | 10 | Base reward for walking |
| XP per Hex Stolen | 25 | Higher reward for PvP |
| XP per km Walked | 50 | Rewards distance |
| XP Streak Bonus | 20 | Daily streak incentive |
| XP All Missions Bonus | 100 | Complete all 3 daily missions |
| Missions per Day | 3 | Manageable daily target |
| Level Formula | (n-1)² × 100 | Quadratic scaling |

---
sectionContent.Security Model:
| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|-----------|
| GPS spoofing | 3-layer anti-cheat (speed + duration + smoothness) |
| Token forgery | Firebase JWT validation (RSA signature + issuer/audience) |
| Rate abuse | 20 claims/day + API-level rate limiting |
| Injection | Parameterized EF Core queries only. No raw SQL. Input validation at boundaries. |
| Unauthorized access | JWT [Authorize] on all mutation endpoints |
| BOLA / IDOR (cross-user reads) | Missions/XP endpoints enforce self-only access via `DenySelf` (403 when caller ≠ route user) — abb321a, CRITICAL-2. AchievementsController still pending same audit. |
| Account deletion | Full GDPR cascade: `DeleteUserData` explicitly purges all 8 child tables (cells, transfers, claims, leaderboard entries, explored cells, daily missions, achievements, device tokens) — no DB-level FK cascades exist, so explicit purge is mandatory (abb321a, CRITICAL-3) |
| Data in transit | HTTPS enforced (ngrok/production TLS) |
| Cooldown bypass | Server-enforced cooldown check. Client cannot override. |

sectionContent.✅ Fully Implemented:
- Territory capture (full pipeline: GPS → anti-cheat → H3 → DB → broadcast)
- SignalR real-time updates with region-based subscription
- **Delta-push architecture (5 state slices + per-user SignalR groups + hydration on login)**
- **Step claim with real-time push (claim → stats/xp/missions/achievements pushed per step)**
- **Victim notification via SignalR (hexCount decremented in real-time when hex stolen)**
- Anti-cheat (3-layer path validation on loop claims **+ per-hop validation on the batch-step path** — abb321a)
- Resilient SignalR broadcasts (per-region failure isolation + non-throwing personal pushes — abb321a)
- Real walked distance tracked on the batch-step path (feeds Distance achievement, leaderboard, WalkDistance mission — abb321a)
- Crash-safe offline claim queue (on-disk WAL with atomic write + backoff drainer + permanent-vs-transient failure handling — abb321a; writes serialized via a write-lock so a concurrent enqueue/rewrite can't drop a queued point — PR #17, regression-tested in PR #25)
- Background-capable GPS tracking (Android foreground service + iOS background updates keep the path recording with the screen off — PR #26, issue #20)
- Offline login persistence (identity-bound `ProfileCache` lets an authenticated user enter offline; restore gated on Firebase UID to prevent cross-user session inheritance — PR #24)
- Offline last-known data (same identity-bound, file-backed cache pattern as `ProfileCache`): owned hexes render on the Start Journey map via `TerritoryCache` (PR #44, issue #33, in review); Daily Mission + Area Exploration home cards via `GameStateCache` (PR #45, issue #34, approved). Cross-user guard + cleared on sign-out/account-deletion. See skill `offline-first-user-bound-cache`.
- Offline journey-start guard (blocks Start Journey when the server is unreachable, since hex capture is server-authoritative — PR #43, issue #35, in review)
- Push notifications (FCM integration, theft alerts)
- Leaderboard (city/country/world, daily refresh, achievement counters)
- User profiles (public + own, tier badges, player titles)
- Walk history (paginated)
- Bot territory seeding (6 cities)
- "End walk without capture" (just-stop feature)
- Revenge tracking (stolen hex history)
- Cell ownership history
- Account deletion (GDPR)

- Dual map themes

content.markdown:
# MyLoop — Product & Technical Spec

## What Is MyLoop?

**MyLoop is a real-world territory capture game.** Players physically walk to claim hexagonal grid cells on a shared world map. Walk a loop → everything inside becomes yours. Others can steal your territory by walking through it — but you get notified and can reclaim.

Think: **Pokémon GO meets Risk meets Strava** — but instead of catching creatures or recording fitness, you're conquering and defending real geographic territory against other players in your city.

---

## Core Gameplay Loop

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Open App] --> B[See Map with Territory]
    B --> C[Tap START JOURNEY]
    C --> D[Walk a Physical Loop]
    D --> E{Loop Detected?}
    E -->|Yes| F[STOP & CAPTURE]
    E -->|No| G[End Walk / Discard]
    F --> H[Server: Anti-Cheat Validation]
    H --> I[Server: H3 Hex Computation]
    I --> J[Server: Assign Ownership + Record Transfers]
    J --> K[Real-Time Broadcast to All Players in Area]
    K --> L[Push Notification to Victims]
    J --> M[Update Leaderboard Position]
    M --> B
```

**What makes it addictive:**
1. You SEE territory on the map — visceral ownership
2. Others can STEAL it — creates urgency to defend
3. Daily streaks + leaderboard rank — competitive drive
4. Physical activity required — can't cheat from couch (anti-cheat enforced)
5. Local competition — city-level leaderboards make it personal

---

## Feature Inventory

### 1. Territory Capture (Core)
- Walk physically. GPS tracks your path at 5-second intervals.
- Close a loop (path endpoints within 50m) → all hexes inside the polygon are captured
- Trail cells (hexes you walk through) are always claimed regardless of loop
- Loop interior fill: closed polygon → H3 fill algorithm claims all hexes inside
- **Min walk: 200m.** Max area per claim: 5 km². Max 20 claims/day.
- 5-hour cooldown on captured cells (anti-grief: prevents instant re-steal)
- Last-writer-wins conflict model (physical presence = ownership)
- Stolen hexes logged for revenge tracking (who took what, when)

### 2. Real-Time Territory Updates (SignalR) — IMPLEMENTED
- WebSocket connection to `/hubs/territory` backend hub
- Connects ONCE on login (after Firebase auth), lives app-lifetime
- Players auto-subscribe to geographic regions (H3 resolution-3 parent cells, ~12km zones)
- Personal group subscription (`user_{userId}`) for private stat deltas
- When anyone claims territory nearby, your map updates instantly via `HexOwnershipChanged` event
- Personal pushes: `UserStatsDelta`, `XpDelta`, `MissionDelta`, `AchievementUnlocked`
- Victim pushes: `UserStatsDelta` with decremented hexCount when hex is stolen
- Reconnection logic with automatic re-subscription + full re-hydrate
- Region subscription updates dynamically as you pan the map
- No [Authorize] on hub class — supports mixed auth (public regions + authenticated personal groups)
- Hub validates token in `JoinUserGroup` before adding to personal group

### 3. Anti-Cheat System (3-Layer Server Validation)
- **Speed check**: Consecutive GPS points must be physically walkable (≤30 km/h, ≤60m per 5s interval). Allows 5% violations for GPS drift.
- **Duration check**: Path must have ≥50% of expected GPS samples for the distance walked
- **Smoothness check**: Bearing standard deviation must be >2°. Real GPS has natural jitter; spoofed linear paths are suspiciously smooth.
- **Batch-step path coverage (abb321a)**: the real-time batch-step claim path (the PRIMARY way players claim) is now validated too, via `ValidateConsecutivePoints` — each GPS hop is bounded by `MaxSpeed × elapsedTime + 30m` drift margin using real `CapturedAt` timestamps; rejected with `400 Anti-cheat: …` over the same 5% tolerance. Previously only loop claims were checked, so a spoofer could teleport on the batch path.
- Rejects GPS spoofers, car drivers disguised as walkers, teleportation hacks

### 4. Push Notifications (Territory Theft Alerts)
- Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) on iOS + Android
- Triggered when another player steals your hexes
- Message: "Territory Under Attack! ⚔️ — {PlayerName} captured {N} of your hexes!"
- Creates urgency to defend → drives re-engagement

### 5. Leaderboard System
- **Scopes**: City / Country / World
- Daily refresh: ranks all players by owned hex count
- Top 20 displayed + your own rank always visible
- Achievement counters increment on rank thresholds (top 3/10/100/1000)
- 7-day history retention for trend analysis

### 6. Progression System (Daily Missions + XP/Levels + Achievements)

**XP & Levels:**
- XP earned from: hex capture (10), hex steal (25), per km (50), streak bonus (20), all-missions bonus (100), individual mission completion, achievement unlocks (25–1000)
- Level formula: `(n-1)² × 100` XP per level. Level 10 = 8,100 XP. Level 50 = 240,100 XP.
- Level displayed in UI, used for achievement thresholds

**Daily Missions (3 per day, adaptive):**
- Generated per user per day using deterministic seed (same missions on reload)
- 6 types: CaptureHexes, WalkDistance, StealHex, ExploreNewArea, MaintainStreak, CaptureInOneWalk
- Adaptive difficulty: Player tier (Newcomer/Regular/Veteran/Elite) × behavior weights → weighted selection
- All-missions bonus: 100 XP when all 3 complete in one day
- Progress tracked in real-time during walks

**Achievements (30 permanent badges, 7 categories):**
- Capture (7): 1→5000 hexes captured
- Streak (6): 3→100 consecutive days
- Distance (5): 1→500 km walked
- PvP (4): 1→100 hexes stolen from others
- Level (4): Level 5/10/25/50
- Leaderboard (2): 1/10 top-3 finishes
- Missions (3): 7/30/100 all-missions-complete days
- Unlocked permanently, award XP (25–1000), shown as badges on profile
- Convergence loop handles cascading unlocks (achievement XP → level → level achievement)

**Architecture:**
- Single-save-point pattern: missions + achievements + XP all saved in one `SaveChangesAsync`
- Concurrent-safe: `DbUpdateException` caught at save point, conflicting achievement inserts detached
- Denormalized counters: `TotalHexesStolen`, `AllMissionsCompleteDays` on User entity
- Checked on every hex capture (negligible perf: 30 int comparisons)

### 7. Revenge System
- See who stole your hexes (last 30 days)
- Grouped by attacker — "Player X stole 47 hexes from you"
- Navigate back to stolen locations and reclaim
- 7-day revenge window for priority recapture

### 8. Walk History
- Paginated list of all past claims
- Shows: cell count, area captured, date
- Infinite scroll with lazy loading

### 9. User Profiles
- Emoji-based avatar system (50+ avatars)
- 8 territory colors (player's hexes render in their color)
- Public profile viewable from leaderboard (stats, rank, title, tier badge)
- Account deletion (GDPR compliance)

### 10. Map Visualization
- **Dual themes**: Satellite (ESRI World Imagery) + Dark (CartoDB)
- **Hex rendering**: User hexes at 20% opacity fill + solid border, other players' hexes colored by owner
- **Tap-to-inspect**: Tap any hex → see owner, claim date, ownership history
- **Follow mode**: Auto-center on GPS, toggle with re-center button
- **Wide-area preload**: Load all user hexes + ~1km viewport on app open
- **Active walk trail**: Green polyline showing current GPS path

### 11. Bot Territory System (Cold Start)
- Pre-populated territory in major cities (Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, London, NYC, Tokyo)
- 10 bot players with realistic hex clusters (~200 hexes each)
- Creates immediate competition for day-1 players in supported cities
- Bots have varied stats, colors, and territory sizes

---

## Technical Architecture

### Stack

| Layer | Technology | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Mobile | Flutter 3.44 / Dart 3.12 | Single codebase for iOS + Android. Fast iteration. |
| Backend | .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core) | High-performance, SignalR built-in, EF Core for DB. |
| Database | PostgreSQL 18 | GiST spatial indexes, reliable, free. |
| Spatial Grid | H3 (Uber) via pocketken.H3 | Global hexagonal grid. Hierarchical (res 3→11). Consistent cell sizes worldwide. |
| Real-Time | SignalR (WebSocket) | Built into ASP.NET, auto-fallback to long-polling, group-based broadcast. |
| Auth | Firebase Authentication | Free, handles Google/Apple OAuth, JWT tokens. |
| Push | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Cross-platform, free tier covers millions of messages. |
| Map Tiles | ESRI + CartoDB (free) | No API key, no billing, unlimited tiles. |
| State Mgmt | Riverpod 3.x | Modern Flutter state. Compile-safe. Reactive. |
| Navigation | go_router + ShellRoute | URL-based, tab persistence via IndexedStack. |
| Dev Tunnel | ngrok | Mobile testing without same-WiFi. Instant HTTPS. |

### Backend Architecture (SOLID)

```
Controllers (thin) → Services (business logic) → EF Core (data access)
         ↑                    ↑                         ↑
   Input validation    Interface-backed         PostgreSQL
   Route → Service     Constructor-injected     GiST spatial index
   ≤20 lines          ≤40 lines per method
```

**Services**:
- `TerritoryService` — Claim processing pipeline (validate → compute → assign → push deltas → broadcast)
- `HexGridService` — H3 computation (point-to-cell, loop extraction, polygon fill, boundaries)
- `PathValidationService` — Anti-cheat (speed, duration, smoothness checks)
- `TerritoryNotifier` — SignalR push to region groups (public hex changes) + user groups (personal deltas)
- `PushNotificationService` — FCM push to victims
- `UserService` — Registration, profile CRUD, account deletion
- `LeaderboardService` — Daily rank computation, scoped queries
- `MissionService` — Daily mission generation, progress recording, XP awarding
- `AchievementService` — Achievement checking with convergence loop
- `GeoService` — Haversine distance, bearing calculations
- `ValidationService` — Input sanitization

### Database Schema

```mermaid
erDiagram
    Users {
        uuid Id PK
        text FirebaseUid UK
        text DisplayName
        text Color
        int AvatarId
        int HexCount
        int TotalHexesCaptured
        int TotalHexesStolen
        int Streak
        int MaxStreak
        float DistanceKm
        int TopThreeFinishes
        bigint TotalXp
        int Level
        int AllMissionsCompleteDays
        text City
        text Country
    }
    TerritoryCells {
        bigint CellId PK "H3 index"
        uuid OwnerId FK
        uuid ClaimId FK
        timestamp ClaimedAt
        timestamp CooldownExpiresAt
        float CenterLat
        float CenterLng
        bigint ParentCellId "H3 res-3"
        text BoundaryJson
    }
    Claims {
        uuid Id PK
        uuid UserId FK
        int CellCount
        float AreaM2
        text PolygonJson "GPS path"
        timestamp CreatedAt
    }
    CellTransfers {
        uuid Id PK
        bigint CellId FK
        uuid FromUserId FK "null = new claim"
        uuid ToUserId FK
        uuid ClaimId FK
        timestamp TransferredAt
    }
    LeaderboardEntries {
        uuid Id PK
        uuid UserId FK
        date Date
        int CellCount
        int Rank
    }
    DeviceTokens {
        uuid Id PK
        uuid UserId FK
        text Token "FCM token"
        text Platform
    }
    DailyMissions {
        uuid Id PK
        uuid UserId FK
        date Date
        int Type "MissionType enum"
        int TargetValue
        int CurrentProgress
        int XpReward
        timestamp CompletedAt "null if incomplete"
        text Description
    }
    UserAchievements {
        uuid Id PK
        uuid UserId FK
        text AchievementId "matches constants"
        timestamp UnlockedAt
        int XpAwarded
    }

    Users ||--o{ TerritoryCells : owns
    Users ||--o{ Claims : makes
    Users ||--o{ CellTransfers : receives
    Claims ||--o{ CellTransfers : generates
    TerritoryCells ||--o{ CellTransfers : history
    Users ||--o{ LeaderboardEntries : ranked
    Users ||--o{ DeviceTokens : devices
    Users ||--o{ DailyMissions : earns
    Users ||--o{ UserAchievements : unlocks
```

### Communication Patterns

| Pattern | Technology | Data Flow | Use Case |
|---------|-----------|-----------|----------|
| **Request/Response** | HTTP REST (Dio + ASP.NET) | Mobile → API → DB → Mobile | Claims, viewport queries, profiles, leaderboard |
| **Real-Time Push (Public)** | SignalR WebSocket | Server → Region Group Clients | Territory ownership changes (instant map updates) |
| **Real-Time Push (Personal)** | SignalR WebSocket | Server → User Group Client | Stats/XP/Mission/Achievement deltas after claims |
| **Background Push** | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Server → FCM → Device OS → App | "Your hex was stolen" notifications (even when app closed) |
| **Auth Token** | Firebase JWT | Mobile → Firebase → JWT → API (Bearer header) | Every authenticated API call (auto-refresh every hour) |
| **Geo Subscription** | SignalR Groups | Client joins H3 parent cell groups | Only receive broadcasts for your visible map area |

### Real-Time State Architecture (Delta-Push) — IMPLEMENTED

**Design principle**: HTTP for writes (reliable), SignalR for pushing consequences (fast).

```
                  SignalR /hubs/territory
                  ──────────────────────
App login ────► Connect ONCE, lives forever (not per-screen)
              ├─► JoinUserGroup("user_{myId}")     ← personal events
              ├─► JoinRegion(parentCellId)          ← visible map area
              └─► Auto-reconnect + re-hydrate on resume
```

**Event Flow After Step Claim:**
```
1. Client HTTP POSTs /api/claims/step (reliable, retryable)
2. Server processes: hex ownership + XP + missions + achievements (single transaction)
3. Server pushes (AFTER SaveChanges succeeds):
   → Region group: HexOwnershipChanged (map update for all nearby)
   → Claiming user group: UserStatsDelta + XpDelta + MissionDelta + AchievementUnlocked
   → Victim user group (if steal): UserStatsDelta (hexCount--)
   → FCM to victim (background notification)
4. Client applies deltas to state slices — no extra HTTP round-trip
```

**State Slices (Flutter — 5 independent Notifiers, ALL IMPLEMENTED):**

| Slice | Provider | Data | Hydrated On Login | Updated Via Push |
|-------|----------|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Profile | `profileSliceProvider` | hexCount, streak, distanceKm, rank, totalHexesCaptured, totalHexesStolen | ✅ | `UserStatsDelta` |
| XP | `xpSliceProvider` | totalXp, level, progressXp, neededXp, progressPercent | ✅ | `XpDelta` |
| Missions | `missionsSliceProvider` | 3 daily missions + progress, allComplete | ✅ | `MissionDelta` |
| Achievements | `achievementsSliceProvider` | unlocked list | ✅ | `AchievementUnlocked` |
| Exploration | `explorationSliceProvider` | neighborhood coverage % | ✅ | On-demand only (no push) |

**Hydration orchestrator**: `hydrateAllSlices(ref)` in `hydration.dart` — calls `GET /api/users/{id}/game-state`, distributes response to all 5 slice notifiers via `.hydrate()` method.

**Deleted**: `game_state.dart` (monolithic GameState + GameStateNotifier) — replaced by 5 independent slices.

### Algorithm Deep-Dive: Claim Processing

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant M as Mobile
    participant API as .NET API
    participant PV as PathValidator
    participant HG as HexGridService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant SR as SignalR Hub
    participant FCM as Firebase Push

    M->>API: POST /api/claims {userId, path[][]}
    API->>PV: Validate(path) — speed, duration, smoothness
    PV-->>API: valid (or reject with reason)
    API->>HG: ComputeCapturedCells(path)
    Note over HG: 1. Trail cells (path intersects)
    Note over HG: 2. Extract loops (closure ≤50m)
    Note over HG: 3. Fill polygon interior (H3.Fill)
    Note over HG: 4. Deduplicate overlaps (>80%)
    HG-->>API: Dict cellId → boundary
    API->>DB: BEGIN TRANSACTION
    Note over API,DB: Batch-load existing cells (single query)
    Note over API,DB: Skip cooldown cells, skip self-owned
    Note over API,DB: Upsert cells + create transfers
    Note over API,DB: Update user stats (hex count, streak, distance)
    Note over API,DB: Decrement victim hex counts
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    API-->>M: ClaimResponse {cellCount, area, boundaries}
    API->>SR: BroadcastOwnershipChanges(region groups)
    SR-->>M: HexOwnershipChanged event (all nearby clients)
    API->>FCM: NotifyVictimsOfTheft(grouped by victim)
    FCM-->>M: Push: Territory Under Attack!
```

### H3 Hexagonal Grid System

**Why H3?**
- Uniform hexagons worldwide (unlike lat/lng grid which distorts at poles)
- Hierarchical: res-11 cells (25m edge) nest into res-3 parents (~12km zones)
- Polygon fill: given any closed shape, H3 returns all hexes inside it
- Deduplication: each hex has ONE globally unique ID — no overlap ambiguity
- Spatial grouping: parent cells naturally partition the world into SignalR broadcast zones

**Resolution 11 choice:**
- Edge length: ~25-29m
- Area per cell: ~2,150 m²
- Feels earnable: a typical city block walk captures 20-50 hexes
- Not too granular (res 12+ would require excessive walking for visible territory)

### GPS & Location Strategy

- **Tracking only during active capture** — battery-friendly, privacy-respecting
- **5-second sampling interval** — enough resolution for path shape, not excessive data
- **Accuracy filter**: Reject readings with accuracy > 25m
- **Speed-aware noise floor**: Stationary = 10-25m clamp, moving = 6-20m clamp
- **Distance filter**: Only record if displacement > 10m (prevent GPS drift accumulation)
- **"When In Use" permission only** — required for Apple App Store approval

---

## Game Constants

| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| H3 Resolution | 11 | ~25m edge. Walkable, visible, not too granular. |
| H3 Parent Resolution | 3 | ~12km zones. Good SignalR broadcast scope. |
| Min GPS Points | 10 | Path must have substance |
| Min Walk Distance | 200m | Prevents trivial tap-and-claim abuse |
| Max Claim Area | 5 km² | Prevents city-wide single-claim exploits |
| Max Claims/Day | 20 | Fair daily cap |
| Cell Cooldown | 5 hours | Anti-grief window |
| Loop Closure Distance | 50m | How close endpoints must be to detect a loop |
| Min Loop Points | 20 | Loop must represent real walking |
| Min Fill Area | 5,000 m² | Ignore tiny interior loops |
| Overlap Dedup Threshold | 80% | Skip near-duplicate polygons |
| Max Speed (Anti-Cheat) | 30 km/h (8.33 m/s) | Walking/jogging speed ceiling |
| Speed Violation Tolerance | 5% | Allow GPS jumps |
| Bearing StdDev Minimum | 2° | Catch linear spoofed paths |
| Max Viewport Cells | 500 | API response size cap |
| Max User Territory Cells | 2,000 | Per-user query limit |
| Leaderboard Top Count | 20 | Visible ranks |
| Revenge Window | 7 days | Time to reclaim stolen hexes |
| XP per Hex Captured | 10 | Base reward for walking |
| XP per Hex Stolen | 25 | Higher reward for PvP |
| XP per km Walked | 50 | Rewards distance |
| XP Streak Bonus | 20 | Daily streak incentive |
| XP All Missions Bonus | 100 | Complete all 3 daily missions |
| Missions per Day | 3 | Manageable daily target |
| Level Formula | (n-1)² × 100 | Quadratic scaling |

---

## Security Model

| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|-----------|
| GPS spoofing | 3-layer anti-cheat (speed + duration + smoothness) |
| Token forgery | Firebase JWT validation (RSA signature + issuer/audience) |
| Rate abuse | 20 claims/day + API-level rate limiting |
| Injection | Parameterized EF Core queries only. No raw SQL. Input validation at boundaries. |
| Unauthorized access | JWT [Authorize] on all mutation endpoints |
| BOLA / IDOR (cross-user reads) | Missions/XP endpoints enforce self-only access via `DenySelf` (403 when caller ≠ route user) — abb321a, CRITICAL-2. AchievementsController still pending same audit. |
| Account deletion | Full GDPR cascade: `DeleteUserData` explicitly purges all 8 child tables (cells, transfers, claims, leaderboard entries, explored cells, daily missions, achievements, device tokens) — no DB-level FK cascades exist, so explicit purge is mandatory (abb321a, CRITICAL-3) |
| Data in transit | HTTPS enforced (ngrok/production TLS) |
| Cooldown bypass | Server-enforced cooldown check. Client cannot override. |

---

## External Services & Costs

| Service | Monthly Cost | Scale Limit | Alternative at Scale |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------------|
| Firebase Auth | $0 | Unlimited users | Keep forever |
| Firebase Messaging | $0 | ~1M messages/month | Keep forever |
| PostgreSQL (self-hosted) | $0 | Single machine | Managed (Neon, Supabase, RDS) |
| ESRI Tiles | $0 | Unlimited non-commercial | Mapbox/MapTiler for commercial |
| CartoDB Tiles | $0 | Unlimited | Self-host OpenMapTiles |
| ngrok (dev) | $0 | 1 tunnel, rate limited | Cloud hosting (Railway, Fly.io) |
| GitHub | $0 | Unlimited private | Keep forever |
| **Total** | **$0** | — | — |

**Production hosting estimate**: Railway/Fly.io ($5-25/month) + managed Postgres ($10-50/month) = **$15-75/month** for first 10K users.

---

## API Surface

### Territory (`/api/territories`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| GET | `/api/territories?minLat&minLng&maxLat&maxLng` | Viewport hex query (max 500) |
| GET | `/api/territories/stats/{userId}` | User's cell count + area |
| GET | `/api/territories/stolen/{userId}?days=7` | Hexes stolen from user |
| GET | `/api/territories/history/{cellId}` | Full ownership history of a hex |
| GET | `/api/territories/user/{userId}` | ALL user's hexes (no viewport limit) |
| GET | `/api/territories/claims/{userId}` | User's walk/claim history |

### Claims (`/api/claims`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| POST | `/api/claims` | Submit territory claim (GPS path — loop/trail) |
| POST | `/api/claims/step` | Single-step hex claim (during active walk) |
| POST | `/api/claims/batch-step` | Batched step claims drained from offline WAL (anti-cheat validated) |
| POST | `/api/claims/trail` | Trail/loop claim (end of walk) |
| POST | `/api/claims/preview` | Preview which hexes path would capture (no DB write) |

### Users (`/api/users`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| POST | `/api/users/register` | Create account (post-Firebase-auth) |
| GET | `/api/users/{id}` | Get user by ID |
| GET | `/api/users/by-uid/{firebaseUid}` | Lookup by Firebase UID |
| PATCH | `/api/users/{id}` | Update profile (name, avatar, color) |
| GET | `/api/users/{id}/profile` | Rich public profile + rank |
| GET | `/api/users/{id}/game-state` | Full state hydration (all 5 slices in one call) |
| DELETE | `/api/users/{id}` | Delete account + all data |
| POST | `/api/users/{id}/device-token` | Register FCM push token |
| GET | `/api/users/{id}/claims?page&pageSize` | Paginated claim history |

### Leaderboard (`/api/leaderboard`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| GET | `/api/leaderboard?lat&lng&userId&scope` | Get ranked players (city/country/world) |
| POST | `/api/leaderboard/refresh` | Recompute daily rankings |

### Missions (`/api/missions`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| GET | `/api/missions/{userId}` | Get/generate today's 3 missions |
| GET | `/api/missions/xp/{userId}` | XP info (total, level, progress %) |

### Achievements (`/api/achievements`)
| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| GET | `/api/achievements/{userId}` | All 30 achievements with progress |

---

## Implemented vs Remaining

### ✅ Fully Implemented
- Territory capture (full pipeline: GPS → anti-cheat → H3 → DB → broadcast)
- SignalR real-time updates with region-based subscription
- **Delta-push architecture (5 state slices + per-user SignalR groups + hydration on login)**
- **Step claim with real-time push (claim → stats/xp/missions/achievements pushed per step)**
- **Victim notification via SignalR (hexCount decremented in real-time when hex stolen)**
- Anti-cheat (3-layer path validation on loop claims **+ per-hop validation on the batch-step path** — abb321a)
- Resilient SignalR broadcasts (per-region failure isolation + non-throwing personal pushes — abb321a)
- Real walked distance tracked on the batch-step path (feeds Distance achievement, leaderboard, WalkDistance mission — abb321a)
- Crash-safe offline claim queue (on-disk WAL with atomic write + backoff drainer + permanent-vs-transient failure handling — abb321a; writes serialized via a write-lock so a concurrent enqueue/rewrite can't drop a queued point — PR #17, regression-tested in PR #25)
- Background-capable GPS tracking (Android foreground service + iOS background updates keep the path recording with the screen off — PR #26, issue #20)
- Offline login persistence (identity-bound `ProfileCache` lets an authenticated user enter offline; restore gated on Firebase UID to prevent cross-user session inheritance — PR #24)
- Offline last-known data (same identity-bound, file-backed cache pattern as `ProfileCache`): owned hexes render on the Start Journey map via `TerritoryCache` (PR #44, issue #33, in review); Daily Mission + Area Exploration home cards via `GameStateCache` (PR #45, issue #34, approved). Cross-user guard + cleared on sign-out/account-deletion. See skill `offline-first-user-bound-cache`.

sectionContent.Offline-First User-Bound Cache:
A repeatable pattern for "show last-known data when the server is unreachable" in MyLoop.
Used for the offline profile (`ProfileCache`, #19), owned hexes (`TerritoryCache`, #33),
and home cards (`GameStateCache`, #34). When a new screen goes blank offline because its
only data source is a server call, add one of these — don't special-case the widget.
sectionContent.When to Activate:
- A screen/card shows nothing offline because its data comes only from an API call.
- You're adding a new offline fallback or a file-backed cache on the Flutter client.
- Reviewing a PR that adds a cache, an offline branch, or a `getX() returns null offline`.
sectionContent.The Pattern (mirror `ProfileCache`):
A **static, file-backed** service in `mobile/lib/shared/services/{name}_cache.dart`:
- **`save(userId, payload)`** — write JSON to the app documents dir on a *successful*
  fetch. Best-effort: wrap I/O in try/catch and **log + swallow** (caching never breaks
  the screen). Never cache an empty `userId`.
- **`load(userId)`** — read it back, returning `null` if absent/unreadable/another user's.
- **`clear()`** — delete the file. **Wire into every `ProfileCache.clear()` call site**
  (sign-out + account-deletion in `auth_service.dart`, `home_screen.dart`,
  `profile_screen.dart`). Missing one leaks data across accounts.
- **Pure `encode` / `decode`** statics so the codec is unit-testable without the filesystem.
- Store the **raw server JSON shape** the consumer already parses (add a model `toJson`
  that round-trips its `fromJson` exactly) — no new serialization to drift.
sectionContent.Non-Obvious Rules (these are what review:
1. **Cross-user binding guard.** Bind the cache to the server `userId` and reject a
   mismatch in `load`/`decode`. Without it, a second account on a shared device inherits
   the first user's data offline. This is the #1 thing to verify.
2. **Restore only when you don't already have fresher data.** Guard the restore (e.g.
   `if (userOwnCellIds.isEmpty)`) so a live/partial load isn't clobbered by stale cache.
3. **Discriminate offline from real errors.** Restore-from-cache should fire on genuine
   connectivity loss, not every exception. Use the existing `isServerUnreachable(e)`
   primitive (`api_service.dart`) and **log/rethrow** non-connectivity failures — a blanket
   `catch (_)` masks a 5xx/parse bug behind stale cache. (If the API method already
   collapses offline to a *logged* `null` — like `getGameState` — consuming that null is
   fine; the discrimination + log already happened at the source.)
4. **Scope the restore.** Only restore the slices in scope (e.g. missions + exploration,
   not achievements) — stale state that misleads the user is worse than an empty card.
5. **Best-effort writes never throw.** A cache write failure must not break hydration/render.
sectionContent.Test Shape:
- Pure codec: round-trip, malformed → null, cross-user → null.
- Disk durability: stub `path_provider` (see `flutter-disk-concurrency-test`), `save` then
  fresh `load` yields the exact pinned set (disk == memory); cross-user `load` → null; clear.
- **Fails-without-fix regression**: drive the real consumer offline (API throws / returns
  null) and assert the slice/state is restored — must fail against the pre-fix empty branch.

# Offline-First User-Bound Cache

A repeatable pattern for "show last-known data when the server is unreachable" in MyLoop.
Used for the offline profile (`ProfileCache`, #19), owned hexes (`TerritoryCache`, #33),
and home cards (`GameStateCache`, #34). When a new screen goes blank offline because its
only data source is a server call, add one of these — don't special-case the widget.

## When to Activate
- A screen/card shows nothing offline because its data comes only from an API call.
- You're adding a new offline fallback or a file-backed cache on the Flutter client.
- Reviewing a PR that adds a cache, an offline branch, or a `getX() returns null offline`.

## The Pattern (mirror `ProfileCache`)
A **static, file-backed** service in `mobile/lib/shared/services/{name}_cache.dart`:
- **`save(userId, payload)`** — write JSON to the app documents dir on a *successful*
  fetch. Best-effort: wrap I/O in try/catch and **log + swallow** (caching never breaks
  the screen). Never cache an empty `userId`.
- **`load(userId)`** — read it back, returning `null` if absent/unreadable/another user's.
- **`clear()`** — delete the file. **Wire into every `ProfileCache.clear()` call site**
  (sign-out + account-deletion in `auth_service.dart`, `home_screen.dart`,
  `profile_screen.dart`). Missing one leaks data across accounts.
- **Pure `encode` / `decode`** statics so the codec is unit-testable without the filesystem.
- Store the **raw server JSON shape** the consumer already parses (add a model `toJson`
  that round-trips its `fromJson` exactly) — no new serialization to drift.

## Non-Obvious Rules (these are what reviews catch)
1. **Cross-user binding guard.** Bind the cache to the server `userId` and reject a
   mismatch in `load`/`decode`. Without it, a second account on a shared device inherits
   the first user's data offline. This is the #1 thing to verify.
2. **Restore only when you don't already have fresher data.** Guard the restore (e.g.
   `if (userOwnCellIds.isEmpty)`) so a live/partial load isn't clobbered by stale cache.
3. **Discriminate offline from real errors.** Restore-from-cache should fire on genuine
   connectivity loss, not every exception. Use the existing `isServerUnreachable(e)`
   primitive (`api_service.dart`) and **log/rethrow** non-connectivity failures — a blanket
   `catch (_)` masks a 5xx/parse bug behind stale cache. (If the API method already
   collapses offline to a *logged* `null` — like `getGameState` — consuming that null is
   fine; the discrimination + log already happened at the source.)
4. **Scope the restore.** Only restore the slices in scope (e.g. missions + exploration,
   not achievements) — stale state that misleads the user is worse than an empty card.
5. **Best-effort writes never throw.** A cache write failure must not break hydration/render.

## Test Shape
- Pure codec: round-trip, malformed → null, cross-user → null.
- Disk durability: stub `path_provider` (see `flutter-disk-concurrency-test`), `save` then
  fresh `load` yields the exact pinned set (disk == memory); cross-user `load` → null; clear.
- **Fails-without-fix regression**: drive the real consumer offline (API throws / returns

yaml.author: robin

sections: Prove a Flutter disk/concurrency regression test by reverting the fix

sectionContent.When to Activate:
Writing a regression test for a Flutter service that persists to disk
(write-ahead log, cache) and/or serializes async operations — especially when the
service uses `path_provider`.
sectionContent.Pattern:
- **Stub `path_provider` with the platform interface, not a method-channel mock.**
  Subclass `PathProviderPlatform with MockPlatformInterfaceMixin`, override
  `getApplicationDocumentsPath` to return a `Directory.systemTemp.createTemp(...)`
  path, and assign it to `PathProviderPlatform.instance` in `setUp`; delete the temp
  dir in `tearDown`. Add `path_provider_platform_interface` + `plugin_platform_interface`
  to `dev_dependencies` so the imports don't trip `depend_on_referenced_packages`.
- **Test the durability invariant, not just memory.** After an awaited batch of
  operations, reopen a fresh instance that reads only from disk and assert it equals
  the live in-memory view — AND assert the exact expected surviving set. (disk==memory
  alone can pass on a regression that drops *everything*, leaving both empty.)
- **Force the race deterministically.** Fire the conflicting ops without awaiting
  between them (`Future.wait([rewrite, append, append])`) and loop ~25 iterations.
- **Prove the test catches the bug.** Temporarily restore the pre-fix source
  (`git show <fix>^:path > file`), run the test, confirm it FAILS, then restore the
  fixed version. A regression test that never fails without the fix guards nothing.

content.markdown:
# Prove a Flutter disk/concurrency regression test by reverting the fix

## When to Activate
Writing a regression test for a Flutter service that persists to disk
(write-ahead log, cache) and/or serializes async operations — especially when the
service uses `path_provider`.

## Pattern
- **Stub `path_provider` with the platform interface, not a method-channel mock.**
  Subclass `PathProviderPlatform with MockPlatformInterfaceMixin`, override
  `getApplicationDocumentsPath` to return a `Directory.systemTemp.createTemp(...)`
  path, and assign it to `PathProviderPlatform.instance` in `setUp`; delete the temp
  dir in `tearDown`. Add `path_provider_platform_interface` + `plugin_platform_interface`
  to `dev_dependencies` so the imports don't trip `depend_on_referenced_packages`.
- **Test the durability invariant, not just memory.** After an awaited batch of
  operations, reopen a fresh instance that reads only from disk and assert it equals
  the live in-memory view — AND assert the exact expected surviving set. (disk==memory
  alone can pass on a regression that drops *everything*, leaving both empty.)
- **Force the race deterministically.** Fire the conflicting ops without awaiting
  between them (`Future.wait([rewrite, append, append])`) and loop ~25 iterations.
- **Prove the test catches the bug.** Temporarily restore the pre-fix source
  (`git show <fix>^:path > file`), run the test, confirm it FAILS, then restore the
  fixed version. A regression test that never fails without the fix guards nothing.

sections: Mobile background location: foreground service vs ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION

sectionContent.When to Activate:
Reviewing or writing any Flutter/geolocator code that must keep receiving GPS
positions while the app is backgrounded or the screen is off (walk tracking,
fitness, navigation).
sectionContent.Rules / Checklist:
- **Android — prefer a foreground service, not background-location permission.**
  Configure geolocator's `AndroidSettings.foregroundNotificationConfig` so it runs
  a location-typed foreground service (visible notification). This keeps the stream
  alive with the screen off and **does not require `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`** —
  omitting that permission keeps you out of Google Play's background-location
  declaration/review policy. Declare `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`.
- **iOS — `allowBackgroundLocationUpdates: true` throws at runtime without
  `UIBackgroundModes: location` in `Info.plist`.** CI/unit tests will not catch
  this. When reviewing a PR that sets it, **verify `Info.plist` directly** (also
  needs `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`; add `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`
  if you want "Always"). Set `pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically: false` so updates
  don't stop when the device is still, and `showBackgroundLocationIndicator: true`.
- **Make the settings selection pure and testable.** A `buildSettings(platform)`
  function that returns the right `AndroidSettings`/`AppleSettings`/`LocationSettings`
  is unit-testable per platform; the actual background behavior is not and needs
  on-device QA (confirm the FGS notification clears when tracking stops; watch
  battery from `enableWakeLock: true`).
- **Store consoles (not code):** App Store Connect App Privacy + Play Console Data
  safety must declare location collection before release — flag these; they can't be
  verified from the repo.

content.markdown:
# Mobile background location: foreground service vs ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION

## When to Activate
Reviewing or writing any Flutter/geolocator code that must keep receiving GPS
positions while the app is backgrounded or the screen is off (walk tracking,
fitness, navigation).

## Rules / Checklist
- **Android — prefer a foreground service, not background-location permission.**
  Configure geolocator's `AndroidSettings.foregroundNotificationConfig` so it runs
  a location-typed foreground service (visible notification). This keeps the stream
  alive with the screen off and **does not require `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`** —
  omitting that permission keeps you out of Google Play's background-location
  declaration/review policy. Declare `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`.
- **iOS — `allowBackgroundLocationUpdates: true` throws at runtime without
  `UIBackgroundModes: location` in `Info.plist`.** CI/unit tests will not catch
  this. When reviewing a PR that sets it, **verify `Info.plist` directly** (also
  needs `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`; add `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`
  if you want "Always"). Set `pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically: false` so updates
  don't stop when the device is still, and `showBackgroundLocationIndicator: true`.
- **Make the settings selection pure and testable.** A `buildSettings(platform)`
  function that returns the right `AndroidSettings`/`AppleSettings`/`LocationSettings`
  is unit-testable per platform; the actual background behavior is not and needs
  on-device QA (confirm the FGS notification clears when tracking stops; watch
  battery from `enableWakeLock: true`).
- **Store consoles (not code):** App Store Connect App Privacy + Play Console Data
  safety must declare location collection before release — flag these; they can't be
  verified from the repo.

## Key Behaviors
City-wide daily leaderboard showing top players by area captured. Updates at 00:00 local time. Shows top 3 prominently, user's own rank, and nearby ranks. Scoped by city for MVP; neighborhood and global scopes planned for later.

# Current Architecture

### Components
- **Daily Batch Job**: CRON job at 00:00 local time computes leaderboard from `territories` table.
- **Leaderboard Snapshots Table**: Stores daily rankings. Query: `SELECT owner_id, COUNT(*) as cells, COUNT(*) * 2150.0 as area_m2 FROM territories GROUP BY owner_id ORDER BY cells DESC`
- **API Endpoint**: `GET /api/leaderboard?city={city_id}&date={date}` — returns top N + user's rank.
- **Display**: Top 3 shown prominently with avatars. User's own rank always visible. Nearby ranks (±2) shown.

### Known Behaviors
- Refreshes once daily at 00:00 local time (not real-time)
- Scoped by city for MVP
- Area = cell count × 2,150 m² (H3 resolution 11 average cell area)
- Ties broken by: earliest claim timestamp (first to reach that cell count wins)
- No Redis needed for MVP — simple DB query on snapshot table

### Edge Cases
- Multi-timezone: when going global, schedule per-city batch jobs using city timezone
- User joins mid-day: appears on next day's leaderboard
- User loses all territory: still appears with 0 (or minimum rank display threshold?)
- City boundaries: use H3 resolution 3-4 parent cells to define city zones

- `mobile/lib/features/leaderboard/leaderboard_screen.dart` — Top 3 podium + ranking list, tappable rows open user profile, Expanded podium items (responsive), `go_router` import for navigation. Each player row has a small colored hexagon icon (`Icons.hexagon, size: 14`) before the name — color matches their `HexTier.fromHexes(hexCount).color`. Tier visible at a glance without text.

## Integration Points
- Reads from `territories` table (owned cells per user)
- Batch job writes to `leaderboard_snapshots` table
- API serves from snapshot table (fast reads, no live aggregation)
- Push notification when user enters top 3

sectionContent.Components:
- **GPS Tracking Service (client-side)**: `LocationService` class in `shared/services/location_service.dart`. Uses `geolocator` package (+ `geolocator_web` for browser). Throws descriptive errors for permission states.
- **Background-capable tracking (client-side, PR #26)**: `startTracking()` builds platform-specific settings via the pure `buildTrackingSettings(LocationPlatform)` so position updates keep arriving with the screen off (issue #20). Android → `AndroidSettings` with a `foregroundNotificationConfig` (geolocator runs a location-typed **foreground service**). iOS → `AppleSettings` with `allowBackgroundLocationUpdates: true`, `pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically: false`, `showBackgroundLocationIndicator: true`. web/other → plain `LocationSettings`. Android manifest declares `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` and deliberately **omits** `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` (a foreground service does not need it; avoids Play background-location review). iOS relies on `UIBackgroundModes: [location]` already in `Info.plist`.
- **Journey Controller (client-side)**: Riverpod `Notifier` pattern (modern, NOT deprecated StateNotifier). State: `JourneyState` with `isTracking`, `path` (List<LatLng>), `distance`, `duration`, `error`. Try/catch wraps all operations. **GPS drift filtering**: rejects accuracy > 25m, uses speed-aware noise floor (stationary: 10-25m, moving: 6-20m), only records to path/distance when displacement exceeds noise floor.
- **Real-time hex display (client-side)**: App shows all hexagons on the map. As user walks, hexes that are >50% inside their trail/loop turn their color in real-time.
- **Trail + Fill mechanic (simplified)**: Two rules only. (1) Trail cells: any H3 cell whose center the path crosses through → claimed. (2) Interior fill: if path forms a closed loop AND enclosed area ≥ 5,000m², any H3 cell whose center is inside the loop polygon → claimed. NO boundary intersection/overlap check. No 51% rule.
- **H3 Computation (server-side, .NET)**: Uses pocketken.H3 v4.0.0 NuGet package at **Resolution 11** (edge ~29m, area ~2,150m²). `ComputeCapturedCells()` orchestrates trail tracing + polygon fill via focused helper methods (all ≤40 lines). Decomposed into: `AddTrailCells`, `AddLoopFillCells`, `ExtractLoops`/`FindClosureLoops`, `BuildRepairedPolygon`, `DeduplicatePolygons`/`IsDuplicateOf`, `FillPolygonInteriors`. **CRITICAL**: `pocketken.H3`'s `LatLng` constructor expects **radians**, not degrees. Must convert: `latRad = latDeg * Math.PI / 180.0`. The `ToLatLng()` method returns a `LatLng` with `.LatitudeDegrees`/`.LongitudeDegrees` properties for conversion back. `FillPolygon` via NTS `.Fill()` handles conversion internally.
- **Perfect Hex Boundaries (server-side)**: `GetPerfectHexBoundary(lat, lng, radiusMeters=25)` generates visually-perfect regular hexagons. Uses `cos(latitude)` correction for longitude degree offsets. All hexes worldwide are exactly 25m radius (center-to-vertex), flat-top orientation. H3's raw boundaries are NOT used for rendering (they distort at high latitudes).
- **Minimum Fill Area (server-side)**: `GeoService.CalculatePolygonArea()` uses Shoelace formula in metric coordinates. Loops < 5,000m² only get trail cells. (Reduced from 30,000m² because resolution 11 cells are smaller — 5,000m² keeps fill viable for reasonable walks.)
- **Claim API (server-side)**: `POST /api/claims` with path → `ClaimsController` validates → `TerritoryService.ProcessClaim` orchestrates → `HexGridService.ComputeCapturedCells` computes trail + fill → stores in PostgreSQL. `ClaimResult` uses static factory: `ClaimResult.Failure(error)`, `ClaimResult.Succeeded(data)`.
- **Step Claim API (server-side)**: `POST /api/claims/step` with single lat/lng → `TerritoryService.ProcessStepClaim` → creates Claim entity → assigns hex → updates stats → pushes personal deltas via SignalR → pushes victim delta if stolen. Returns `StepClaimResponse` with cellId, boundary, xpGained, achievements, wasStolen, previousOwnerName.
- **Trail Claim API (server-side)**: `POST /api/claims/trail` with path → `TerritoryService.ProcessTrailClaim` → creates Claim entity → assigns all trail + fill cells → updates stats → pushes all deltas. Same push pattern as step claim but batched.
- **Claim Entity Creation (CRITICAL)**: Both `ProcessStepClaim` and `ProcessTrailClaim` MUST create a `Claim { Id, UserId, CellCount, AreaM2 }` entity BEFORE inserting `TerritoryCell` records. FK constraint: `TerritoryCells.ClaimId → Claims.Id`. Omitting this causes PostgreSQL FK violation.
- **Post-Claim Push Pipeline**: After `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds, TerritoryService calls:
  1. `PushPersonalDeltas(userId)` → fires UserStatsDelta, XpDelta, MissionDelta, AchievementUnlocked to claiming user's SignalR group
  2. `PushVictimDelta(victimId)` → fires UserStatsDelta to victim's SignalR group (decremented hexCount)
  3. `NotifyHexOwnershipChanged(changes)` → fires to region groups (public map update)
  4. FCM notification to victim (background theft alert)
- **Service Architecture (SOLID)**: All services have proper interfaces (`IHexGridService`, `ITerritoryService`, `IUserService`, `ILeaderboardService`, `IGeoService`, `IValidationService`). All dependencies constructor-injected. No method exceeds 40 lines. One class per file.
- **Constants**: All magic numbers extracted to `GameConstants` class — `MinLoopPoints`, `LoopSkipNeighbors`, `DeduplicationOverlapThreshold`, `MinFillAreaSquareMeters`, `CellCooldownHours`, etc.
- **Cell Cooldown**: A cell cannot be re-stolen within `CellCooldownHours` (5 hours) of its last transfer. Anti-grief mechanic.
- **User Territories API**: `GET /api/territories/user/{userId}` — returns ALL cells owned by user (no viewport limit). Used by mobile map to guarantee user always sees their hexes regardless of current GPS location.
- **Claim History API**: `GET /api/territories/claims/{userId}` — returns chronological claim history (ClaimId, CellCount, AreaM2, Date). Used by home page "Hex History" widget.
- **Claim Flow (client-side)**: All claim logic lives in `_JourneyScreenState._onStopCapture()` — NOT in child widgets. Uses lifecycle-stable `context` for dialogs. Reads fresh state via `ref.read()` to avoid stale closures. Sequence: submitClaim → showCapturedHexes → optimistic badge update → forceReloadHexes → getUser → getLeaderboard → updateStats(all 4 fields) → showCelebration.
- **Frontend decomposition**: `LoopDetector` (static class, mirrors backend ExtractLoops), `HexTerritoryManager` (hex loading/state management), `CelebrationDialog` (standalone widget). JourneyScreen extracted: `_CircleButton`, `_HexOwnerSheet`, `_StatsBar`, `_BottomControls`. Map build split into focused methods.
- **Conflict Resolution (server-side)**: Last-writer-wins. Walking through someone's hex steals it.
- **Ownership History**: `CellTransfers` table logs every ownership change with `FromUserId`, `ToUserId`, `ClaimId`, `TransferredAt`. `TerritoryCell.PreviousOwnerId` stores last owner for fast single-query lookups. Powers the "revenge recapture" feature (Clash of Clans model: raid → lose hexes → see what was taken → go reclaim).
- **Spatial Indexing**: `TerritoryCell` stores `CenterLat` + `CenterLng` (double) for viewport queries. See spatial index decision section below.
- **Anti-cheat on batch-step path (server-side, abb321a)**: `IPathValidationService.ValidateConsecutivePoints((Lat,Lng,CapturedAt)[])` now guards the real-time batch-step claim path (the PRIMARY way players claim). Bounds each GPS hop by `AntiCheatConstants.MaxSpeedMetersPerSecond * elapsedSeconds + 30m` drift margin using the real `CapturedAt` timestamps; rejects when implausible-hop rate exceeds the existing 5% tolerance. Wired into `ClaimBatchStep` → `400 {error:"Anti-cheat: ..."}`. Previously only loop claims were validated, so a spoofer could teleport on the batch path.
- **Real walked distance on batch path (server-side, abb321a)**: `ProcessBatchStep` now computes real GPS distance via `IGeoService.CalculatePathDistance` for the slice and adds it to `Users.DistanceKm` (recomputed per retry → no double counting). Real metres also feed the `WalkDistance` mission. Previously only the loop path incremented `DistanceKm`, so walk-and-claim players had `DistanceKm=0`.
- **Resilient SignalR broadcasts (server-side, abb321a)**: `NotifyHexOwnershipChanged` wraps each region send in its own try/catch (one failed region no longer aborts the rest); personal-delta pushes go through a generic `SafeSendToUser<T>` that logs and never throws (fire-and-forget pushes can no longer surface as unobserved task exceptions).
- **Offline claim queue + crash-safe WAL (client-side, abb321a)**: GPS step points are appended to an on-disk write-ahead log (`StepClaimQueue`) and drained in batches by `BatchDrainService` (exponential backoff 1s→30s). `StepClaimQueue` uses `_atomicWrite` — write to a sibling `.tmp`, flush, then atomically `rename` over the target — so a crash mid-write can only leave an ignored temp file, never a truncated/lost WAL.
- **WAL write serialization (client-side, PR #17)**: Every disk-mutating `StepClaimQueue` op (`enqueue` append, `removeProcessed`/`clear` rewrite) runs through a `_writeLock` future chain (`_synchronized`). Without it, an `enqueue` append can interleave with a rewrite: the rewrite snapshots the cache, the append lands on the file, then the rewrite's atomic `rename` replaces the file with a snapshot lacking the just-appended point — losing a queued GPS point if the OS kills the app. Regression test added in PR #25 (`step_claim_queue_test.dart`): proven to fail against the pre-#17 unserialized version and pass with the lock.
- **Permanent vs transient batch failures (client-side, abb321a)**: `claimBatchStep` distinguishes 4xx (throws `BatchRejectedException` carrying the server message via `extractApiError`) from 5xx/offline (returns null → retry with backoff). The drainer drops permanently-rejected points, resets backoff, and emits the reason on `onRejection`, which the journey controller surfaces via its existing `error` state. Previously every error collapsed to null and a poisoned batch (e.g. the new anti-cheat 400) would retry forever silently.
sectionContent.Known Behaviors:
- H3 Resolution 11: ~29m edge, ~2,150m² area per cell. Smaller than res 10 — feels more earnable per walk.
- Territory = set of H3 cell IDs (64-bit integers) owned by a user
- Capture = trail (center of hex within path corridor) + fill (center of hex inside closed polygon). NO boundary intersection checks.
- Loop closure: path self-intersection detected via `FindClosureLoops` (point within 50m of earlier non-adjacent point). NOT just first-to-last.
- GPS accuracy: ±5-15m outdoor clear, ±20-50m urban obstructed
- Minimum path length: 200m (anti-abuse)
- Maximum claim area: 5km² per claim (anti-abuse)
- Rate limit: max 20 claims per day per user
- **pocketken.H3 LatLng expects RADIANS** — passing degrees produces cells at wrong locations (typically shifted towards higher lat/lng values, e.g., Bangalore → Pacific/Japan). Only `AddTrailCells` needs manual conversion; `FillPolygonInteriors` via NTS `.Fill()` handles it internally.
- H3 Cell IDs are 64-bit integers (~15 digits at res 11). Safe on mobile Dart (64-bit int) but overflows JavaScript `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53) on web. Not a blocker for iOS-first.
- **Deduplication**: Overlapping polygons (>80% area shared) are deduplicated before fill to prevent double-counting.
- **Loop detection constants**: `MinLoopPoints=20` (don't bother looking for loops in short paths), `LoopSkipNeighbors=10` (skip adjacent points when searching for crossings).
- **Offline own-hexes cache (client-side, PR #44 / issue #33, in review)**: `HexTerritoryManager.loadUserOwnHexes()` caches the fetched owned set to a file-backed, user-bound `TerritoryCache` on success and restores it when the fetch fails, so the Start Journey map still shows the player's territory offline instead of a blank grid. Cross-user binding guard + cleared on sign-out/account-deletion (mirrors `ProfileCache`, #19). Review-pending change: narrow the blanket `catch` to `isServerUnreachable` so non-offline errors aren't masked. See [[skl-offline-first-user-bound-cache]].
- **Sustained-speed anti-cheat (server-side, PR #42 / issue #37, in review)**: `ValidateConsecutivePoints` adds a window-average gate (`AntiCheatConstants.MaxAverageSpeedMetersPerSecond ≈ 9 m/s`) over the whole batch on top of the per-hop bound. The flat +30 m per-hop GPS-drift margin inflated the effective per-hop ceiling to ~51 km/h, letting a steady ~40 km/h vehicle pass every hop; the batch-average gate rejects sustained vehicle speed the per-hop check misses.
- **Offline journey-start block (client-side, PR #43 / issue #35, in review)**: `JourneyController.startJourney` probes `ApiService.isServerReachable()` (short-timeout GET to the anonymous health endpoint) before any GPS work; offline it sets a clear error (shown via the existing red SnackBar) and does not start. Hex capture is server-authoritative, so starting offline produced no preview/claims/feedback. Mid-journey drops stay handled by the `StepClaimQueue` WAL.
sectionContent.Edge Cases:
- GPS drift creates invalid polygon → path simplification + server validates polygon is valid
- User loses GPS signal mid-capture → client stores last known position, resumes on re-acquisition
- User's path crosses itself → take outer boundary only
- User starts capture, never closes loop → auto-cancel after 4 hours or manual discard
- Two users submit overlapping claims simultaneously → last-to-commit wins (serialized at DB level)
- GPS spoofer teleports on the batch-step path → `ValidateConsecutivePoints` rejects with `400 Anti-cheat: ...` (abb321a); empty / zero-timestamp batches handled without false rejects
- App crashes mid WAL write → `_atomicWrite` (tmp + rename) guarantees the queue is never truncated; only an ignored `.tmp` file can remain
- Concurrent `enqueue` + `removeProcessed`/`clear` on the WAL → serialized by `_writeLock` (PR #17); without it the rewrite's rename clobbers a just-appended point (data loss). Guarded by `step_claim_queue_test.dart` (PR #25)
- Screen off / app backgrounded mid-walk → position stream kept alive by an Android foreground service / iOS background updates (PR #26); pre-fix the path collapsed to a straight line and route hexes were lost (issue #20)
- "While in use"-only location grant → foreground tracking still works; `LocationService` logs a warning that background delivery may be throttled until all-the-time access is granted
- Server permanently rejects a batch (4xx, e.g. anti-cheat) → drainer drops those points, resets backoff, surfaces the reason via `onRejection` (no infinite retry loop)
sectionContent.Problem: Viewport query `GET /api/territories?bounds=...` currently loads ALL cells into memory and filters in C#. Fails at ~5,000+ cells.
sectionContent.Options Evaluated:
| Approach | Index | Truly 2D? | Extension Needed? | Verdict |
|----------|-------|-----------|------------------|---------|
| `(lat, lng)` composite B-tree | B-tree | ❌ 1D primary sort | No | Rejected — lat range scan works, lng is post-filter |
| PostgreSQL native `point` + GiST | GiST | ✅ Yes | No — ships with PG | **Chosen** |
| PostGIS `geometry` + GiST | GiST | ✅ Yes | Yes — PostGIS | Deferred — overkill until Martin tiles needed |
| Geohash (text, B-tree prefix) | B-tree | ✅ Effectively | No | Future option — H3 parent cell is equivalent |
sectionContent.Why composite B-tree on (lat, lng) is wr: B-tree sorts by lat first, lng second. A bounding box query gets efficient lat range scan, but lng is evaluated as a post-scan filter on every row in the lat band — not a true 2D operation. Degrades badly at city scale.
sectionContent.Chosen: PostgreSQL native `point` + GiST:
- `point` type ships with PostgreSQL — no extension to install
- GiST index on `point` column = true 2D spatial index (both dimensions used in tree traversal)
- Viewport query: `WHERE center <@ box '((lng1,lat1),(lng2,lat2))'`
- Maps to `NpgsqlPoint` in .NET, zero extra dependencies
sectionContent.Why PostGIS is deferred (not rejected fo:
PostGIS becomes the right choice when:
1. **Martin vector tiles** are adopted — Martin reads PostGIS geometry columns directly
2. Complex spatial ops needed (polygon buffers, distance queries, etc.)
Adding a `geometry` column later is a non-breaking migration. No wasted work.
sectionContent.Extensibility Path:
```
Now:      CenterLat/Lng doubles + GiST on point column
Later:    + PostGIS geometry column  →  Martin vector tiles
Future:   + Geohash column (text)    →  prefix sharding
Always:   H3 parent cell (ParentCellId, res 3) stored  →  H3-native hierarchy queries
```

`ParentCellId` (H3 resolution 3, stored as `long`) is a native H3 geohash equivalent. It costs one int64 per row and enables partition-style queries by area without any extension. H3 cell IDs are a spatial hash by design.
sectionContent.CellTransfers table (NEW):
```
CellTransfers
├── Id (Guid PK)
├── CellId (bigint FK → TerritoryCells)
├── FromUserId (Guid? — null means was previously unclaimed)
├── ToUserId (Guid FK → Users)
├── ClaimId (Guid FK → Claims)
├── TransferredAt (timestamp)
└── INDEXES:
    (FromUserId, TransferredAt DESC) — "hexes stolen from me, most recent first"
    (ToUserId, TransferredAt DESC)   — "hexes I've captured"
    (CellId)                         — "full history of this hex"
```
sectionContent.Queries this enables:
- `"Show me my stolen hexes"` → `WHERE FromUserId = me AND TransferredAt > 7d ago`
- `"Who keeps raiding me?"` → `GROUP BY ToUserId WHERE FromUserId = me ORDER BY count DESC`
- `"Most contested hex in city"` → `GROUP BY CellId ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC`
- `"Territory I've held longest"` → `TerritoryCells WHERE OwnerId = me ORDER BY ClaimedAt ASC`
- `"Revenge: recapture within 24h"` → `WHERE FromUserId = me AND TransferredAt > 24h ago AND current OwnerId != me`
sectionContent.PreviousOwnerId on TerritoryCell (fast p: Dual approach: `CellTransfers` for full audit trail, `PreviousOwnerId` on the cell itself for single-query "who did I steal this from?" — avoids a JOIN for the common case.
